authors: McComb, K., Shannon, G., Durant, S.M., Sayialel, K., Slotow, R., Poole, J., Moss, C.
title: Leadership in elephants: the adaptive value of age
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
data_extracted: 72 playbacks across 39 family groups; mean 5±2.6 adults/family; matriarchs 23-70y range; oldest matriarchs (60+) show greater sensitivity to male-vs-female lion threat; bunching intensity correlation rho=0.90 p<0.0001 with matriarch age; 1,500 Amboseli individuals in 58 family groups

authors: McComb, K., Shannon, G., Sayialel, K.N., Moss, C.
title: Elephants can determine ethnicity, gender, and age from acoustic cues in human voices
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (cited via PMC3874604 review)
data_extracted: Amboseli ~1500 indiv/58 families undisturbed; Pilanesberg ~200/16 families founded from culling survivors; 274 playbacks (165 Amboseli, 109 Pilanesberg); Amboseli alien-caller discrimination p=0.01; Pilanesberg failed (p=0.50); age discrimination Amboseli p<0.001 vs Pilanesberg p=0.99; long-term culling effects evident decades later

title: Social play in African savannah elephants may inform selection against aggression
data_extracted: 15 elephants; 230.5 obs hours; 52 aggression bouts (22.6/100h); play age correlation r=-0.738, p=0.002; males > females in play (p=0.028); aggression more BETWEEN than within families (p=0.002); 4 family units + 2 solitary males

title: Reduced older male presence linked to increased rates of aggression to non-conspecific targets in male elephants
data_extracted: 1527 focal follows (281 individuals 2015-2018); 68.5% follows zero aggression; older male presence (26+y bulls) reduces aggression coefficient=-0.242 p=0.001; adolescents 2.62x adults aggression when isolated (p=0.021); group composition data

title: Knowledge transmission, culture and the consequences of social disruption in wild elephants
journal: Phil Trans Roy Soc B / Review
data_extracted: Review of 95 papers (81 savannah, 8 Asian, 6 forest); 67 papers note sociality changes; 50 demographic impacts; 33 papers poaching; calf mortality highest in primiparous mothers; matriarch knowledge as key resilience factor

title: Social and genetic connectivity despite ecological variation in a killer whale network
journal: Proc Roy Soc B / Curr Biol
data_extracted: 457 photo-ID individuals; 548 encounters 2008-2021; modularity Q=0.68; 27 communities; mean community size 11.0±5.9; SRI 0.19±0.19 range 0.03-1.0; 501 strong dyads (10% non-zero); kinship odds ratio 3.976 (1.526-10.328); within-community relatedness 0.075

title: Mortality risk and social network position in resident killer whales
data_extracted: Male hazard ratio 0.33±0.2 for high closeness; 0.21±0.14 for high within-community degree; female no significant network effect; whales together 1-149 times/yr mean 5±7.9; median 6 communities/yr (range 5-9); 11±5.9 indiv/community; mortality strongly predicted male survival in low salmon years

title: Infanticide in a mammal-eating killer whale population
data_extracted: ONE confirmed event Dec 2, 2016; 5300+ photographically documented encounters since 1973; perpetrators 32y male (T068A) + 46+y mother (T068); victim neonate <2 days (T046B5) from young mother (T046B 28y); West Coast Transient population several hundred individuals; growth 3%/yr since 1975

title: Age and sex influence social interactions, but not associations, within a killer whale pod
data_extracted: Southern resident KW UAS aerial study; age/sex did NOT detectably influence association network structure; significant social homophily by age and sex in synchronous surfacing and contact networks; contact centrality higher in females and young

title: Revised Age Estimates for Northern Resident Killer Whales based on observed life-history events and demographic discounting
data_extracted: 96 individuals revised; females observed with offspring averaged 5.0y younger than prior estimates; males immature at study start 1.9y younger; female age at first reproduction ~10y; fecundity decreases after age 40; post-reproductive lifespan revised down

authors: Holekamp, K.E., Sakai, S.T., Lundrigan, B.L.
title: Social intelligence in the spotted hyena (Crocuta crocuta)
data_extracted: Clan size 6-90 indiv (large clans 70+); linear matrilineal hierarchy; extremely stable over years; rank acquired by 18mo following mother; non-littermates inverse-age rank; reconciliation 15% of fights; males reconcile more than females; coalitions almost always join dominant side

title: Long-term demography of spotted hyena in Liuwa Ecosystem
data_extracted: 663 individual hyenas in 11 clans 2010-2019; density 0.68/km² dry, 0.69/km² wet (range 0.18-1.01); cubs F survival 0.76 M 0.75; sub-adults 0.99; adults F 0.86 M 0.82; cub mortality 23.5%; 13 known deaths in 10y; 4 directly observed lion kills

title: Food availability and male deference in the female-dominant ring-tailed lemur, Lemur catta
data_extracted: Male deference rates: St Catherine low-provisions 51-62%; high-provisions 69-74%; LA Zoo 2016-17 70%; female-to-male agonism per hour: low-prov 5.2±0.8 (range 4.5-6.4); high-prov 4.6±0.8 (range 4.0-5.1)

title: Androgen levels and female social dominance in Lemur catta
data_extracted: Beza Mahafaly two groups; 2301 agonistic interactions in 1800h (1.28/h); 86% over food; females won 96.9% of agonistic interactions with males; only 37% of female wins lacked female aggression

title: The Island of Female Power? Intersexual Dominance Relationships in the Lemurs of Madagascar
data_extracted: Table 1: 36 lemur entries; nearly all female-dominant except P. simus + M. myoxinus; Lemur catta 0.49 conflicts/h; female win rates 0-100% by species; SSD mean 0.97±0.09; SSD negatively correlated with female-win-rate

authors: NPR (reporting on Smith et al. 2026 Sci Adv)
title: No coup, just cuddles. A naked mole rat colony changes queens peacefully
journal: NPR news + Smith et al. Science Advances 2026
data_extracted: Single peaceful queen succession documented April 2026; previously thought all transitions lethal; colonies typically 60-300; queen suppresses ovulation in all other females; aggression initiated by queen + breeding males; shoving primary aggression mode

title: Dominance and queen succession in captive colonies of the eusocial naked mole-rat
data_extracted: Captive colonies; queen removal results in social instability and aggression between high-ranking individuals; dominance rank predictor of reproductive status; queens highest-ranking, succeeded by next-highest females

title: Lethal aggression in Pan is better explained by adaptive strategies than human impacts
data_extracted: 152 killings across 18 chimp + 4 bonobo communities; bonobos NOT observed to kill in any community; foundational for round-1 round-2 lethal-partition signature

authors: Wrangham, R.W., Wilson, M.L., Muller, M.N.
title: Comparative rates of violence in chimpanzees and humans
data_extracted: 125/100k/y pooled chimp intergroup lethal rate; baseline for round-2 comparison

title: Drivers of female power in bonobos
data_extracted: 6 wild bonobo communities 30y; Kokolopori females dominate 98.4% of conflicts; 85% of female coalitions target males; matriarchy via coalition

authors: Tokuyama, N., Sakamaki, T., Furuichi, T.
title: Inter-group aggressive interaction patterns indicate male mate defense and female cooperation across bonobo groups at Wamba
data_extracted: 3 neighboring bonobo groups Wamba; female cross-group cooperation documented; female-female intergroup aggression RARE; key bonobo anomaly = matriarchy via coalition despite male-philopatry
